defects.where: data/paper-ledger.json plan.objective + phases[0].units_by_price; index.html 1225-1261 and 1328-1345 versus 964-1028
defects.what: Two contradictory unit prices on one tab. The UNITS table and the ROUTES table run on the ledger's hand anchor 2.25 + 0.25 x (MSTX - 14); LeapsCost runs Black-Scholes calibrated to real prints. At today's MSTX 18.73 the anchor gives 3.43 and the real 9/18 print is 4.00. Fitting all six prints gives an intercept near 2.92 against 2.25, so the anchor is about 30% low and every LEAPS count Alex reads off those two tables is overstated roughly 15-25%. The ledger's own routes_note says so and that sentence is truncated off screen.

The Phase 1 panel reads three fields the ledger no longer has (debit_natural, hurdle, odds_short), so both rows print "hurdle unknown", the odds chip never renders, and the footer still explains odds that are not shown. At the same time contracts (275 / 175) and cost ($5,775 / $11,200) are in the ledger and never rendered, so the "what is on" panel does not say how big the position is.

Playbook inputs are 5 days old and there is no scheduler for the refresh script anywhere in the repo. Downstream: the hero word runs on the week-ending-9/06 MACD bar (two weekly bars behind), the MACD chart is 12 days behind, IV rank is as of 9/11, and the events list still contains the 9/16 FOMC which only a client-side filter hides. Meanwhile paper-ledger.json and leaps-cost.json were written today, so the tab silently mixes two different as-of dates.

The Playbook names the ticker and picks its accent color from the LIVE quantile (getTier(q)); the Ladder tab names it from the MONTHLY CLOSE (getTier(qM)), which is Alex's actual rule. Near a band edge the two tabs will claim different tickers on the same day.

The "Rising since X" caption lies when the histogram is falling. The loop walks back only while each bar exceeds the prior one; if the last bar is lower the loop never runs and it returns the last bar's own date, so the page prints "Rising since <latest date>" regardless of direction. It reads correctly today only because the histogram happens to be rising.

All three fetches swallow errors with .catch(() => {}). If playbook.json fails the hero reads UNKNOWN with no explanation; if paper-ledger.json fails the tab reads "No spreads in the ledger" and "No routes in the ledger" as if the positions were flat; if leaps-cost.json fails the whole chart returns null and vanishes. This is a direct cause of "I don't even know if it works properly."

The LEAPS-units objective Alex names as a reason he opens the tab (long Dec 2028 $33 call, short Jan 2028 $60 call, counted in units) exists in the ledger as plan.objective and is rendered nowhere. The instrument is named only in small grey type as the LeapsCost subtitle.

sk() garbles the strike chip: key "Oct 9 16 / Oct 2 16 calendar".split("/")[1] yields " Oct 2 16 calendar", so the chip would read "Oct 2 16 calendar strike · 24% odds". Invisible today only because odds_short is absent from the ledger.
Dead constant: LINE is defined in the playbook helper block and used nowhere in the file.

About 60% of the 14.8KB ledger is fetched on every page load and thrown away: journal (10 entries, 6.1KB), paper_calls (565B), plan.week_of_2026_09_14 (1.4KB), plan.objective, plan.unit_price_anchor_mstx, and per-phase structure, status, positions, note, units_note, dates_note, roll_rules. No history block is rendered at all. One journal entry is dated 2026-09-26, a future date sitting between 9/17 entries.

25.7KB file the page never fetches. It is an input to tools/playbook_refresh.py only, and its last write is 9/13, the same stall as playbook.json. Nothing on the tab is broken by it, but it is not a site data file.

The UNITS slider persists per browser in localStorage (bql_pb_mstx, default 16.4) and spans 13 to 22 in 0.25 steps across only 13 sparse rows, so most drags above 19 snap to the same row and change nothing.
The hero chips scroll to the MACD panel when clicked, including the ladder-quantile chip, which has nothing to do with the panel it jumps to.

minimal_layout: HERO: the word, the phase, the two or three next-action steps, and the refresh age (red past 2 days). No chip row.
PHASE 1 · WHAT IS ON: legs, contracts, debit, dollars in, break-evens, and the 10/2 decision date, straight from the ledger fields that actually exist.

LEAPS UNITS: one panel. Today's real unit price and unit count at the top, the day-by-day cost chart under it, about six by-close rows re-anchored to the print-calibrated price, and TODAY / LOW as the only two reference numbers.
WEEKLY MACD: one compact histogram with the bar date it is really reading, and a caption that only claims 'rising' when it is.
summary: The Playbook tab renders 13 visible blocks and Alex acts on four of them. Cut the hero chip row, the two stat cards and the Phase 2 strike map outright (every one of those either repeats something already on screen or, in Phase 2's case, still describes a 9/18 vertical that no longer exists while Phase 1 above it says the decision date is 10/2). Merge the ROUTES table and five of the seven LeapsCost reference cards into a single units panel. The worst defect is not clutter: the UNITS and ROUTES tables run on a hand unit-price anchor of 2.25 + 0.25 x (MSTX - 14) while the LeapsCost chart directly below them runs Black-Scholes fitted to real prints, and today those disagree by 3.43 versus 4.00 a unit, so the LEAPS counts Alex reads are overstated 15 to 25 percent. The ledger itself flags this in a sentence the page truncates. Second: the Phase 1 panel reads three fields the ledger dropped, so it prints "hurdle unknown" twice while the contract counts and dollars it does have go unrendered. Third, and the reason the site "doesn't feel like it works": playbook.json has not refreshed since 9/13, tools/playbook_refresh.py has no scheduler, and every fetch on the tab swallows its errors silently, so a failed load looks like a flat position rather than a broken page. Ship four sections, not thirteen.
